newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - December 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - December 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- DTI GIVES FINAL PUSH FOR NORTH SEA OIL

The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) have attempted to provide a boost to North Sea oil and gas production by telling oil companies all the remaining unlicensed areas will be open for exploration. The ambitious programme was unveiled by Energy Minister Lord Fraser and his deputy, Richard Page. Huge fiels, which represent two-thirds of the total area designated for licence, will be available for drilling.
-- CUT-PRICE SALE TEED UP BY CLUBPARTNERS

Clubpartners, the golf course operator, admitted it was in talks to sell the company for one pence stg a share. PGA European Tours, operator of some of Europe's smartest championship courses, is tipped to attempt a takeover.

Clubpartners has a debt load of around five million stg, excluding loan stock, partly as a result of funding the purchase of its two existing golf courses and an attempt to buy a third, which was aborted earlier this month.
-- UNITED BISCUITS JETTISONS FROZEN VEGETABLES

United Biscuits has sold its frozen vegetable products business for 44 million stg in cash to a management team backed by UBS. The deal will result in a 52 million stg exceptional charge to this year's profits. The group is writing off 19 million stg for the brand value and 32 million stg for goodwill, and the deal will dilute its earnings in the short term, but the proceeds will be used to repay debts.
THE TIMES
-- BANK ATTACKED OVER BARINGS

A report by the Treasury Select Committee has attacked the Bank of England over its role in the collapse of Barings. It said that banking operations should be taken away from the Bank if it does not change the way it operates. It also attacks the auditors of Barings, the Securities and Futures Authority, and questions the effectiveness of international co-ordination when it comes to supervising financial markets. It recommends that all regulation of the financial markets be taken away from the DTI and given to the Treasury.
-- SHEFFIELD UNITED JOINS STOCK MARKET

Sheffield United is set to become the sixth football club to join the stock market after a 21.5 million stg reverse takeover of Conrad, the leisure group. Conrad will pay 9.5 million stg for the Sheffield and the combined group will launch a 12 million stg rights issue to fund development of United's ground. United hopes to be promoted to the Premiership and is offering share incentives to its football manager, Howard Kendall, and some of the players.
-- BUILDING WORKERS GET FIRED UP FOR NEW YEAR

A survey from Hays Montrose, the recruitment consultant, which specialises in the construction and property industries, asked employees working in building about what they wanted in the new year. More than half want a pay rise, and more than a third are thinking about switching jobs. Fourteen percent are looking forward to firing someone. However, four-fifths of the workers say they expect the jobs situation in the construction industry to be better in 1997 than this year.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BRITISH TELECOM CONFRONTS OFTEL IN COURT

Lawyers for British Telecom have argued in the High Court that the director-general of Oftel, Don Cruickshank, acted unlawfully when he included a catch-all fair trading clause in the telecom group's licence. Oftel insist that new fair trading powers are essential to offset the deregulation of BT's activities. However, BT claims that Cruickshank exceed his authority. BT lawyers said the new clause was unlawful because it would contradict sections of the 1984 Telecommunications Act and would lead to conflict between Oftel and the OFT.
-- MINISTERS OFFER BUILDING SOCIETIES EXTRA PROTECTION

It is expected that the Government's Building Society Bill will offer building societies that become banks an extra safeguard against hostile takeovers. Angela Knight, Treasury minister, hopes the additional protection will placate the three building societies which have threatened to shelve their stock market floatation and halt the payment of seven billion stg in windfall bonuses. The societies are the Alliance and Leicester, Woolwich and Northern Rock.
-- CALL FOR INVESTIGATION INTO RAIL PENSION 'HIGHWAY ROBBERY'

Labour and trade unions have called for an independent investigation to gain clarification from the Government over plans for the 500 million stg surplus from the British Rail pension fund, after claims that the money is to be shared among new railway operators as a privatisation "sweetener". Trade unions called the revelation "highway robbery" and accused the government of breaking its promises that the 10.5 billion stg British Rail pension fund would not be affected by privatisation.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BUMPER PAY RISES FOR GRANADA CHIEFS

Chairman of Granada Group, the media, leisure and rentals conglomerate, Gerry Robinson, has been paid 728,000 stg in the year to September, a rise of 21 percent, and chief executive, Charles Allen, received a 53 percent increase to 531,000 stg. Outgoing chairman, Alex Bernstein, earned just 210,000 stg in his last full year in the position. The higher figures are seen by some as an indication of a change in corporate style at the group.
-- DIGITAL TELEVISION GETS DTI GO-AHEAD

The publication of final regulations from the DTI on set-top box technology will mean the way has been cleared for the launch of 200 digital television channels by late 1997. BSkyB is expected to award contracts to six set-top box manufacturers, including Pace Micro Technology, Sony and Nokia. The boxes will be subsidised by a Sky-led consortium involving Midland Bank, British Telecom and several leading retailers. The DTI also incorporated new safeguards to prevent anti-competitive behaviour.
-- M AND G BACKS 196 MILLION STG BID FOR NEWMAN

The engineering group FKI has launched a hostile 196 million stg takeover of Europe's largest architectural hardware company, Newman Tonks. Newman Tonks' biggest shareholder, M&G, said it had irrevocably undertaken to accept the offer while Britannic Assurance, another institutional investor, pledged its 2.2 percent stake to FKI. This is an unusual move for M&G as the fund manager normally backs management in takeover situations, however the group has become disillusioned with Newman Tonks' poor track record.
